title: Bay Area autumn offers: what to use from October to mid-November
summary: Browse announced store activities, museum free days, birthday and membership perks, and ongoing resources. Filter no-purchase, reservation-based and purchase-required offers, including November dates and still-valid October deals.
keywords: Bay Area autumn offers: what to use from October to mid-November
content:
Check eligibility before planning a pickup

Start with something you will actually use, then check dates and eligibility. Target’s October promotion is not a November Black Friday announcement. Lowe’s November craft date is published, but local slots still require confirmation.

Filter by date, area and redemption conditions

Ended offers are hidden by default. Purchase-required offers are discounts; reservation-based offers require a confirmed slot. Ongoing perks remain subject to account, stock and store terms.

LOWE’S：Pick up a free kids' lollipop while you're there
Ongoing benefit · Ask on each store visit
MyLowe's Rewards members must have created a Kids Profile for their child. No purchase or appointment required, while supplies last.
Ask at the Customer Service Desk for a free organic lollipop. A convenient stop when a parent is already shopping with their child.
Kids Club lollipop perk：https://www.lowes.com/diy-projects-and-ideas/workshops

IKEA：Regular coffee or tea for members
Ongoing benefit · During restaurant hours
Show your IKEA Family barcode; no additional purchase required. Confirm weekend availability and eligible drinks with the store first.
Redeem in the Swedish Restaurant. Bay Area options include Emeryville and East Palo Alto. Restaurant and store hours differ.
IKEA Family hot drink perk：https://www.ikea.com/us/en/ikea-family/

SEPHORA：Pick up a beauty mini gift in store during your birthday month
Birthday month · Once per year · No purchase in store
Join Beauty Insider for free and add your birthday before redeeming. The current official FAQ allows one gift each year during your birthday month. Provide your member email in store; no purchase is required, while supplies last.
Find Bay Area Sephora stores including Emeryville. Online redemption requires at least $25 in qualifying merchandise. Gift choices depend on membership tier and store stock. Older pictured sets do not establish October availability, and extra weeks outside the birthday month are not guaranteed.
Sephora official 2026 birthday gifts and redemption conditions：https://www.sephora.com/beauty/birthday-gift

STARBUCKS：Stay for free refills of eligible coffee and tea
Ongoing benefit · during the same café visit
Buy and enjoy your first drink in the café. Eligible hot or iced brewed coffee and tea refills are available during the same visit at participating stores.
Ask your barista and use a for-here cup. Refills exclude Cold Brew, Nitro, Iced Tea Lemonade, flavored iced tea and Refreshers; lattes are not included either.
Café refill choices and exclusions：https://about.starbucks.com/back-to-starbucks/

CONSERVATORY OF FLOWERS · SF：10/6: Free Conservatory Visit in Golden Gate Park
Oct 6 · 10:00–16:30; last admission at 16:00
General admission is free for everyone on the first Tuesday of each month, not only SF residents. Last entry is at 16:00; special events are separate. Check official entry arrangements before visiting.
100 John F Kennedy Drive. 10/6 follows the official free-day policy. Open until 16:30; the conservatory is normally closed on Wednesdays.
Conservatory Hours and Free-Day Policy：https://gggp.org/visit/admissions-hours/

SAN FRANCISCO BOTANICAL GARDEN：10/13: Free General Admission All Day at the Botanical Garden
10/13 · 07:30–18:00; last admission in October is at 17:00
General admission is free for everyone on the second Tuesday of each month, not only SF residents. Paid special events and programs are excluded. Check official entry arrangements before visiting.
1199 9th Avenue. 10/13 follows the official policy. October's last entry is at 17:00; the garden closes one hour later, at 18:00.
Botanical Garden Free-Day Policy and October Hours：https://gggp.org/visit/admissions-hours/

LOWE’S：Build a free firefighting plane on October 17
Sat 10/17 · 10 AM–1 PM
MyLowe’s Rewards, a child’s Kids Profile and advance registration are required. Recommended for ages 4–11 with an adult. Free; availability varies by store.
The official schedule lists Firefighting Plane on October 17. Choose a nearby Bay Area store and an available session before registering. The September haunted-house workshop has ended.
Firefighting Plane official date and registration：https://www.lowes.com/events/register/firefighting-plane

YOGURTLAND：20% off in-store for members on October 20
Tue 10/20 · Participating store hours
Real Rewards membership and an in-store purchase are required; same-day signup is allowed. Show the app or linked phone number. Cannot be combined with other offers.
The official anniversary offer runs on the 20th of each month in 2026. Confirm your Bay Area store participates on October 20. Online orders, delivery, catering and gift cards are excluded.
Yogurtland monthly anniversary terms：https://www.yogurtland.com/news_posts/view/86/celebrating-20-years-of-yogurtland-anniversary-promo-how-you-can-join-the-fun

SONOMA VALLEY MUSEUM OF ART：Free Wednesday art visits in Sonoma
Every Wednesday · 11 AM–5 PM
Wednesday general admission is free without membership or purchase. Check in at the desk; children under 13 need an adult.
551 Broadway, near Sonoma Town Plaza. October Wednesdays are the 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th; the current M. Louise Stanley exhibition runs through January 24, 2027. Workshops have separate pricing.
Sonoma museum free Wednesdays and closure notice：https://svma.org/visit/

JAPANESE TEA GARDEN · SF：Free Tea Garden Entry During the First Hour on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays
Free admission Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 09:00–10:00
Free entry Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 09:00–10:00, for everyone, with no purchase or SF residency requirement. Tea, refreshments, and special programs cost extra. Check ticket arrangements and temporary opening changes before visiting.
75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive, in Golden Gate Park. Entry after 10:00 does not qualify for this free hour. This is an ongoing policy visible on the official site as of 2026-09-29, with no published end date, not a new September promotion.
Japanese Tea Garden Official Free-Entry Hours：https://gggp.org/visit/admissions-hours/

SAN FRANCISCO PUBLIC LIBRARY：SF residents: reserve museum passes with your library card
Ongoing benefit · Up to two active reservations
Must be a resident of the City and County of San Francisco using a personal SFPL card; Teacher Cards are excluded. Passes are for the named holder on the specified date, with party-size and child-accompaniment rules set by the venue.
A new month is released on the 1st, with up to two active reservations. Confirm travel plans before downloading or printing: either action prevents cancellation. Availability and free or discounted coverage follow the logged-in pass.
SFPL official Discover & Go booking and cancellation rules：https://sfpl.libanswers.com/faq/97385

SAN MATEO COUNTY LIBRARIES：Peninsula museum passes: use the right library portal
Ongoing benefit · Up to two active reservations
Current FAQ: live within the SMCL service area, hold a valid library card and be age 16 or older. eCards and institutional cards are excluded. The named holder needs valid ID on the reserved date.
Cards beginning 29041 or 29731 use the county portal. San Mateo city, Redwood City and other cards use their own library portals. Capacity varies by venue; printed passes cannot be canceled.
SMCL museum-pass eligibility and booking FAQ：https://smcl.org/faq/museum-passes-discover-go/

ALAMEDA COUNTY LIBRARY：East Bay residents: check free or low-cost library passes
Ongoing benefit · Availability shown after login
Age 15 or older, residence within AC Library’s service area, and a full library card are required. eCards are excluded. Price and group size vary by pass.
Readers in places such as Fremont and Dublin can start with their own library portal. Alameda County, Alameda city and Oakland cards are separate, and some passes are discounted rather than free.
AC Library Discover & Go eligibility：https://aclibrary.org/faq/library-cards-ecards/

SANTA CLARA COUNTY PARKS：Borrow a county parks vehicle pass
Ongoing benefit · Three-week checkout
A card from a participating library is required to borrow a physical pass. Covers one passenger vehicle with capacity of 15 or fewer, or one road-legal motorcycle. Stock is limited.
Participating libraries include SJPL, SCCLD, Santa Clara City, Palo Alto, Sunnyvale, Los Gatos and Mountain View. Valid only at Santa Clara County parks; excludes Uvas Canyon, Sunnyvale Baylands, camping and other park systems.
Santa Clara County Library Parks Pass：https://parks.santaclaracounty.gov/library-parks-pass

MUSEUM OF SONOMA COUNTY：Free family day in Santa Rosa on October 10
Sat 10/10 · Activities 11 AM–1 PM
The museum lists a free family day, with activities from 11 AM to 1 PM. Check the event details for the program and participation instructions.
425 Seventh Street, Santa Rosa. Pair the family program with a downtown walk. The hours listed are the official activity window; confirm admission terms for other times.
Museum of Sonoma County official October calendar：https://museumsc.org/events/

SFMOMA · SAN FRANCISCO：10/25: Visit SFMOMA with a Child; Up to Two Adults Enter Free
Sunday 10/25 · 10:00–17:00 · Tickets open two weeks ahead
Up to two adults receive free general admission when accompanying one child or teen age 18 or younger. Surcharged exhibitions require separate paid tickets. Adults attending without a child do not qualify.
The October 25 theme is now K-Pop, Art, and Beyond, including art making, SFPL storytime, a scavenger hunt and a dance party. Tickets open two weeks ahead; up to two adults must accompany one child age 18 or under. Surcharged exhibitions cost extra.
SFMOMA Free Family Day and Adult Admission Limit：https://www.sfmoma.org/free-days/

CANTOR ARTS CENTER · STANFORD：Stanford’s Cantor Arts Center is always free
Ongoing benefit · Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays
Free general admission for the public. Groups of 10 or more must register ahead. Parking, café purchases and dining cost extra.
328 Lomita Drive. Current official hours: Monday and Friday 11 AM–6 PM, Thursday 11 AM–8 PM, weekends 10 AM–5 PM. Check for temporary changes before an October visit.
Cantor free admission and current official hours：https://museum.stanford.edu/visit

SAN FRANCISCO PUBLIC LIBRARY：Borrow a radon detector free with an SFPL card
Ongoing loan service · Up to 21 days
An SFPL card is required; place holds online. Devices are first come, first served, may be borrowed for up to 21 days, and must be returned.
A home-device lending service introduced in 2026, available through all branches and returnable to any branch. Check the catalog and hold queue first; the device is a free loan.
SFPL free device loan announcement：https://sfpl.org/releases/2026/07/15/free-radon-detector-loan-program-promote-home-safety

BERKELEY PUBLIC LIBRARY：Berkeley residents can borrow tools and kitchen equipment free
Ongoing service · Tool Library registration required
Only Berkeley residents or property owners over age 18 qualify. Address or property ownership verification and borrowing paperwork are required; limit 10 items at a time.
1901 Russell Street. Check inventory for drills, gardening tools and selected kitchen equipment. A regular library card does not replace the Tool Library’s residency verification.
Berkeley Tool Library borrowing eligibility：https://www.berkeleypubliclibrary.org/locations/tool-lending-library/borrowing-tools

IKEA EMERYVILLE：An extra 10% off As-is items on Wednesdays at IKEA Emeryville
Every Wednesday · Emeryville store only
Show your IKEA Family member number at checkout. Applies only to marked As-is items; no stacking or previous purchases. As-is items cannot be returned.
4400 Shellmound Street. The current weekly rule gives an extra 10% off on October 7, 14, 21 and 28. Stock varies; no end date is published, so reconfirm before visiting.
IKEA Emeryville As-is Wednesday terms：https://www.ikea.com/us/en/stores/emeryville/

POPPY & CLARO · SAN JOSÉ：Friday outings with your dog: $6 three-course dinners continue into fall
Fall Fridays · Patio, 5–8 PM
The $6 meal is for dogs, on the patio Fridays from 5 to 8 PM, weather permitting. Human food and drinks cost extra; confirm seating and availability with the restaurant.
50 West San Fernando Street. The restaurant has extended the offer into fall. Under its Friday rule, October dates are 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30; no final end date is published.
Poppy & Claro fall Doggie Dinners：https://www.poppyandclaro.com/

HAPPY HOLLOW · SAN JOSÉ：Free Happy Hollow admission for ages 50+ on October 22
Thu 10/22 · Enter 9–10 AM
For ages 50 and older. Senior Safari includes free admission and parking from 9 to 10 AM; enter before 10 AM to stay for the day.
October 22 follows the official fourth-Thursday schedule for May–October 2026. Register on arrival; park at 748 Story Road. Food costs extra; check current parking instructions.
Happy Hollow 2026 Senior Safari：https://happyhollow.org/seniorsafari/

MUIR WOODS · MARIN：Muir Woods entrance fee waiver on October 27
Tue 10/27 · Parking or shuttle reservation required
The 2026 NPS fee-free day applies to U.S. citizens and residents. Parking and shuttle fees remain payable; vehicles and shuttle riders still need reservations.
The official calendar lists Theodore Roosevelt’s birthday on October 27. Confirm a GoMuirWoods slot before planning the redwood walk; the waiver does not replace reservations.
Muir Woods fee-free days and reservation rules：https://www.nps.gov/muwo/planyourvisit/fees.htm

CHABOT · OAKLAND：Free telescope viewing in the Oakland hills
Fridays and Saturdays · 7:30–10:30 PM, weather permitting
Public telescope viewing on the observatory deck is free. Rain, clouds or humidity can affect access; museum admission and ticketed events are separate.
10000 Skyline Blvd. The Friday/Saturday schedule extends through October 30–31. Check Chabot’s weather station and evening notices before leaving, and bring layers.
Chabot free viewing and weather conditions：https://chabotspace.org/programs/free-telescope-viewings/

RANDALL MUSEUM · SAN FRANCISCO：Free family science outings at Randall Museum
Tuesday–Saturday · 10 AM–5 PM
General admission is free with no purchase required. Some classes and workshops cost extra; check the day’s calendar.
199 Museum Way. Pair science and local wildlife exhibits with a nearby walk. Closed Sundays and Mondays; the final October Saturday is October 31.
Randall official hours and free admission：https://randallmuseum.org/faqs/

TRITON MUSEUM · SANTA CLARA：Free exhibitions and parking at Santa Clara’s Triton
Tuesday–Sunday · 11 AM–4:30 PM
Exhibition admission and parking are free; classes and some special events cost extra. Closed Mondays and holidays.
1505 Warburton Avenue. Posted gallery closures: Cowell on October 20, noon–2 PM; Mathias October 29–November 5. Check accessible galleries for a late-month visit.
Triton admission and October gallery notices：https://www.tritonmuseum.org/visit

ANDERSON COLLECTION · STANFORD：Free modern art at Stanford’s Anderson Collection
Thursday–Monday · 11 AM–5 PM
Free public admission; closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Stanford parking charges apply separately.
314 Lomita Drive, near Cantor, makes a useful campus art pairing. Monday opening began in 2026; the two museums have different weekend hours.
Anderson free admission and 2026 hours：https://anderson.stanford.edu/visit/

CURIODYSSEY · SAN MATEO：Eligible Benefit-Card Families: Up to Four Free at CuriOdyssey
Applies on open days. Closed for maintenance on 10/19; closes early at 15:00 on 10/31.
Show photo ID and proof of an officially accepted program, such as EBT/CalFresh/SNAP, WIC, Medicaid, or Medi-Cal, for free admission for up to four people per day. Eligibility is checked at the counter; parking costs extra.
1651 Coyote Point Drive. Closed for maintenance on 10/19; closes early at 15:00 on 10/31. Check special-event ticket rules separately. This is an ongoing policy visible on the official site as of 2026-09-29, with no published end date, not a new September promotion.
CuriOdyssey Eligible Benefit-Card Admission Rules：https://curiodyssey.org/visit/museums-for-all/

EXPLORATORIUM · SAN FRANCISCO：Exploratorium: $5 Admission with an Eligible Benefit Card
Daytime opening hours and 18+ After Dark; follow the day's schedule
Bring an EBT/SNAP/CalFresh, Medi-Cal, or WIC card, or a Lifeline Pass, plus matching photo ID, to buy up to four tickets at $5 each. P-EBT and EBT Sun Bucks are excluded. On-site purchase only.
Pier 15. Valid for daytime admission or After Dark for ages 18 and up; tickets cannot be bought online. This is not free admission; families with children should choose daytime hours. An ongoing policy visible on the official site as of 2026-09-29, with no published end date.
Exploratorium for All: Current Prices and Required ID：https://www.exploratorium.edu/visit/reduced-rates/

LAWRENCE HALL OF SCIENCE · BERKELEY：Up to six free at The Lawrence with an EBT card
Wednesday–Sunday · 10 AM–5 PM
A state-issued SNAP EBT card from any U.S. state and valid photo ID cover the cardholder plus five guests. No advance registration required.
1 Centennial Drive. Collect tickets at Visitor Services. Exhibitions are included; 3D films and some activities cost extra. EBT verifies eligibility and is not charged.
The Lawrence Museums for All six-person rule：https://lawrencehallofscience.org/visitors/plan-your-visit/museums-for-all/

SONOMA COUNTY LIBRARY：Borrow a Sonoma regional-parks parking pass
Ongoing loan · Check availability first
Borrow a Regional Parks day-use parking pass with a Sonoma County Library card. One passenger vehicle with capacity of nine or fewer; camping, commercial use and extra fees excluded.
Check out at a branch or place a catalog hold, then plan a Russian River, coast or Sonoma Valley outing. This county regional-parks pass is separate from the state parks pass.
Sonoma library regional-parks parking pass：https://sonomalibrary.org/browse/libraryofthings/socoparkspass

SONOMA COUNTY LIBRARY：North Bay library passes for free or discounted attractions
Ongoing · Up to two reservations at a time
Sonoma County residents age 15+ need a regular library card and PIN. eCards are excluded; party size and discount depend on the attraction.
Search Discover & Go by date or venue for October availability. Cancel before printing; printed passes cannot be canceled. Check whether each pass is free or discounted.
Sonoma Discover & Go eligibility：https://sonomalibrary.org/node/130

SFMTA · SAN FRANCISCO：Muni buses and trains are free for everyone age 18 and under
Ongoing · No residency or income restriction
Riders age 18 and under need no application or Clipper card for regular Muni service. Ages 16+ should carry age ID. Cable cars are excluded from this general benefit.
Useful for October park and museum outings. San Francisco youth residents can separately apply for a cable-car pass. These rules do not apply to BART or Caltrain.
SFMTA free Muni for youth eligibility：https://www.sfmta.com/fares/free-muni-all-youth-18-years-and-younger

CLIPPER START · BAY AREA：Half-price single rides with eligible Clipper START
Ongoing program · Apply and qualify first
Bay Area residents ages 19–64 with household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level must submit identity and income proof; RTC disability-card holders are excluded.
MTC’s current program gives 50% off single rides on Bay Area agencies accepting Clipper. Use your approved personalized START card; an ordinary bank card does not grant eligibility.
MTC current Clipper START half-fare program：https://mtc.ca.gov/planning/transportation/access-equity-mobility/clipperr-startsm

SFMOMA · SAN FRANCISCO：SF Residents with Eligible Benefit Cards: Up to Four Adults Free at SFMOMA
Applies during opening hours; closed Wednesdays
San Francisco residency is required. Present a valid Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SNAP, or EBT card and proof of residency. Each eligible guest can receive up to four adult tickets, including general admission and special exhibitions.
151 Third Street. Documents are checked on the day of your visit; eligibility does not extend to all Bay Area residents. This differs from the two-adult limit for the 10/25 Family Day. An ongoing policy visible on the official site as of 2026-09-29, with no published end date.
SFMOMA Resident Benefit-Card Admission Terms：https://www.sfmoma.org/deals-discounts/

CABLE CAR MUSEUM · SAN FRANCISCO：See cable-car machinery at the free Cable Car Museum
Tuesday–Sunday · Closed Mondays
Museum admission is free with no cable-car ride or purchase required. Riding a cable car is charged separately under SFMTA fares.
1201 Mason Street. Tuesday–Thursday 10 AM–4 PM; Friday–Sunday 10 AM–5 PM. Pair with a walk around Chinatown or Nob Hill.
Cable Car Museum free admission and hours：https://www.cablecarmuseum.org/info.html

OAKLAND PUBLIC LIBRARY：Tool loans for Oakland, Emeryville and Piedmont residents
Ongoing loan · Seven-day borrowing period
Residents or property owners of these three cities over age 18 must register at the Tool Library. First checkout is limited to two tools; late, damage and replacement fees apply.
5205 Telegraph Avenue. Call 510-597-5089 to place a hold; return tools clean and on time during opening hours. A regular library card does not replace tool-library registration.
Oakland Tool Library eligibility and lending rules：https://oaklandlibrary.org/otll/lending/

ROSIE THE RIVETER · RICHMOND：Free Richmond visit exploring Bay Area home-front history
Ongoing free admission · Check visitor-center hours
The Rosie the Riveter visitor center and Rosie Memorial are free with no park pass required. The partner Red Oak Victory ship has separate admission rules.
The visitor center is at 1414 Harbour Way South, Richmond. Pair it with a waterfront walk; free park admission does not cover every partner site or special program.
NPS Richmond free-admission coverage：https://www.nps.gov/rori/planyourvisit/fees.htm

CHICHA SAN CHEN · NORCAL：Birthday-day drink BOGO at six NorCal shops
Ongoing benefit · On your birthday only
Show a valid physical ID at the shop's front register on your birthday. No preorders. Each transaction is limited to 10 drinks, with multiple transactions allowed. Purchase is required for the complimentary drink.
The official pinned terms cover Cupertino, Berkeley, Daly City, Fremont, San José and Pleasanton. The benefit was still posted on September 23 and can inform October birthday plans under current rules. No end date is published; recheck before visiting.
CHICHA San Chen official pinned birthday BOGO terms：https://www.instagram.com/chichasanchen.norcal/p/DVUxImmkci8/

CHICHA SAN CHEN · CUPERTINO：Reserve a complimentary Lishan oolong tasting in Cupertino
Regular reservation program · Check calendar availability
Free, about 15 minutes and conducted in English. One reservation covers one seat; companions need separate reservations. Check in 10 minutes early.
At 20688 Stevens Creek Boulevard. The official afternoon tasting explores five roast profiles. This complimentary experience is separate from paid tea ceremonies and mocktails. Check calendar availability for October; daily sessions are not guaranteed.
CHICHA San Chen official free tasting reservations and rules：https://chichasanchennorcal.com/reservation/ola/services/lishan-oolong-tea-tasting

AMC · BAY AREA：Half-price adult base movie tickets on Tuesdays and Wednesdays
Ongoing benefit · Tuesday and Wednesday showtimes
AMC Stubs membership is required; the free Insider tier qualifies. Save 50% on the adult evening base ticket price, up to 10 tickets per show date. Tax, online fees and premium-format or special-event surcharges are not halved.
AMC NewPark 12 in Newark lists this benefit on its official page. October's Tuesdays and Wednesdays fall on 6/7, 13/14, 20/21 and 27/28. Check the film, showtime and checkout discount; some films and special events may be excluded.

The Hillsdale store lists the workshops as free, recommended for ages 2–5 with a supervising adult. Confirm local availability and reserve first.
At 341 Hillsdale Mall in San Mateo, monthly hands-on building supports developmental skills. Confirm the booking location from the local store page because generic links may lead out of state. A take-home set is not promised.
LEGO Hillsdale official store page · Free preschool building classes：https://www.lego.com/en-us/stores/store/hillsdale-shopping-center

LEGO MAGAZINE：Free LEGO Magazine by mail for ages 5–9, including postage
Ongoing subscription · Four issues a year; first issue per confirmation email
A parent or guardian subscribes for a child ages 5–9 using a free LEGO account and valid mailing address. No credit card or purchase is required.
Choose Sign up on the official magazine page and enter child and address details. Printing and postage are free. The next issue is listed for November 2026; new subscribers should use their confirmation email for first-delivery timing.
LEGO official free magazine · Age, mailing and subscription rules：https://www.lego.com/en-us/magazine

TODAY AT APPLE · BAY AREA：Free family session: Make Earth-inspired comics on iPad
Free reservation · Choose a Bay Area store and available session
A free Today at Apple session with devices provided. A parent or guardian must stay throughout; an adult meeting the booking requirements must register.
Find Kids: Create Comics Inspired by Planet Earth and create with photos, drawing and stickers on iPad. Select a nearby Apple Store to check dates; sessions are not available at every store every day.
Apple official · Kids Earth-inspired comics session：https://www.apple.com/today/event/workshop-create-comics-inspired-planet-earth/

TODAY AT APPLE · BAY AREA：Free session for ages 6–10: Make an interactive storybook
Free reservation · Dates and remaining spaces vary by store
Recommended for children ages 6–10 and their families. Devices including iPad are provided; a parent or guardian must book and remain throughout.
Select Kids: Create an Interactive Story of Kindness to make a story with drawings, sounds and 3D shapes. Choose a Bay Area store and available time, then follow the booking confirmation.
Apple official · Kids interactive kindness story session：https://www.apple.com/today/event/kids-create-interactive-story-of-kindness/

THE HOME DEPOT：Free kids’ building workshop: Check the next local booking
Ongoing program · Usually first Saturday at 9 AM; check availability
The official Kids Workshops program is free in store, while supplies last. Select a Bay Area store and use Register Now to confirm the session and register.
Build the project announced for your booked session. The Oct 3 event has ended; this is the ongoing booking program. The next project and remaining supplies are unconfirmed, so do not rely on an old poster for kit pickup.
Home Depot official free kids’ workshops and registration：https://www.homedepot.com/c/kids-workshop

WORLD MARKET：Existing Zombie Rewards: $5/$10 off through October 31
Only members already issued this reward · through October 31, 2026
Only accounts already issued a September Zombie Reward qualify: Explorer members receive $5 off $5 in eligible merchandise; Premier members receive $10 off $10. Sign in or provide your member ID. Joining now does not guarantee issuance.
To receive the reward again, eligible merchandise after the reward and other discounts must total at least $15/$25 before tax; reissue takes about 3 days. Otherwise it is used up. All rewards expire at 11:59 p.m. local time on October 31. Alcohol, gift cards, taxes and shipping are excluded. A store is listed in Oakland.
World Market official 2026 Zombie Rewards terms：https://www.worldmarket.com/customer-service/world-market-rewards-rules.html

TACO BELL：New-member app reward: redeem within 14 days
Once per new member · 14 days after issue
Join Taco Bell Rewards and choose a welcome reward in the app, with no purchase required. App orders for in-store or drive-thru pickup only; once per person.
Choose from the current options in the app; upgrades, substitutions and add-ons are excluded. No website orders, delivery or offer stacking. Check participating San Jose locations and availability.
Taco Bell official welcome-offer terms：https://www.tacobell.com/offers-and-deals

McDONALD'S：First app purchase of $1+ includes 10-piece McNuggets
First-time app users · use by the end of the month
First-time app users must opt into MyMcDonald's Rewards, spend at least $1 before tax on their first purchase at a participating location and apply the offer. Once per person; allow up to 48 hours for the offer to appear.
The official offer must be used by the last day of the month; check its exact expiry and location terms in the app. An official store listing is available for Story Road, San Jose. This is the new-user nugget offer, separate from the weekly fries deal.
McDonald's official new-app-user offer：https://www.mcdonalds.com/us/en-us/download-app.html

PEET'S COFFEE：New members earn 125 points on their first scanned order
Once per new member · first qualifying order
Join Peetnik Rewards and scan your first qualifying order to receive 125 points. Downloading the app alone does not unlock a drink. Members enrolled through Peet's Disloyalty are excluded from this welcome bonus.
The official chart offers selected brewed coffee, tea or bakery items at 50 points and selected lattes and other items at 120. Check the app, convert points into a reward, then redeem it. The Market Street store lists Peetnik Rewards participation.
Peetnik Rewards official 2026 terms：https://www.peets.com/pages/peetnik-rewards-terms-and-conditions

PEET'S COFFEE：Birthday drink: account activity required within 180 days
Birthday reward valid 14 days · prior transaction required
Join Peetnik Rewards at least 7 days before your birthday and provide your birthday during registration. A scanned in-store purchase or Mobile Order Ahead order in the previous 180 days is required.
Eligible members receive one birthday drink reward, valid for 14 days; bottled beverages are excluded. Once annually, with eligible choices shown on the reward. The San Francisco Market Street store participates in the rewards program.
Peetnik Rewards official birthday conditions：https://www.peets.com/pages/peetnik-rewards-terms-and-conditions

HABIT BURGER & GRILL：New members: buy an eligible drink, receive a burger
New CharClub members · 14 days after issue
Create a new CharClub account on the website or app and use the welcome offer with an eligible regular-size or larger drink. Shakes, sundaes and other Frozen Treats do not qualify. Once per person/household.
Choose a qualifying Charburger, cheeseburger or veggie burger as offered, without add-ons. Redeem at the register or while logged in online/in-app, not at kiosks or third-party platforms; no stacking. A store is listed in San Jose's Almaden area.
Habit official welcome burger-and-drink terms：https://www.habitburger.com/offer-terms/

HABIT BURGER & GRILL：Chocolate sundae at the register on registration day
CharClub registration day only · register redemption
Create a new CharClub account on the website or app and redeem a Chocolate Sundae at a participating store's register that same day. No purchase required; once per person/household, while supplies last.
Confirm store participation and your account offer before redeeming. Kiosks, app, website and delivery orders are excluded. Cannot be combined with the burger welcome offer or other promotions. Check the San Jose Almaden store before visiting.
Habit official Free Sundae terms：https://www.habitburger.com/offer-terms/

CHIPOTLE：New members: chips and guacamole with a $5+ purchase
New Rewards members · check account expiry
Join Chipotle Rewards as a new member and make a purchase of at least $5 to redeem the Chips & Guac welcome reward through your account at participating stores or official ordering channels.
This welcome offer requires a minimum purchase. The current public page does not give a universal expiry; check the reward's expiry and order restrictions before going. No promotion stacking. An official store is listed on Monterey Highway, San Jose.
Chipotle official Rewards welcome offer：https://www.chipotle.com/rewards

CRUMBL：Birthday dessert reward for Silver members and above
Birthday benefit · reach Silver status for the year
Reach Silver status or above by earning 500 Crumbs during the year to qualify for the Free Single birthday reward. A basic Bronze sign-up does not automatically include a free birthday cookie.
Check your tier, birthday details and issued reward in your account. The voucher controls the redemption period and eligible single dessert. A store is listed on Camden Avenue, San Jose. This benefit requires qualifying rewards status.
Crumbl official reward tiers and birthday benefit：https://crumblcookies.com/rewards

DUNKIN'：Guest-survey coupon: doughnut with a medium-or-larger drink
Guest-survey coupon · 14 days after issue
Complete the official guest satisfaction survey and obtain a valid coupon code. Buy a medium-or-larger Dunkin' beverage at a participating store, excluding cooler beverages, and present the code when ordering. Single use.
Receive one Classic Donut, limited to one coupon per customer per visit. App orders and offer stacking are excluded; applicable tax is extra. An official store page lists 240 El Camino Real in San Carlos; confirm participation first.
Dunkin' official guest-survey redemption rules：https://www.dunkindonuts.com/contact-us/

WORLD MARKET：New members: 15% off the first purchase within 7 days
First Rewards enrollment · 7-day welcome coupon
Be at least 18, join World Market Rewards for the first time with a valid email and create your member ID. Use the welcome coupon within 7 days and identify your rewards membership at checkout.
Valid for an eligible first purchase in-store or online. Gift cards, alcohol, prior purchases, taxes and shipping are among the exclusions; check the coupon. A store is listed in Oakland. This is the free-membership offer and does not require a credit card application.
World Market official Rewards rules：https://www.worldmarket.com/customer-service/world-market-rewards-rules.html

PETSMART：First Autoship order: 35% off, up to $20
First Autoship order · recurring paid orders
Sign in to Treats Rewards and place your first eligible Autoship order for 35% off, capped at $20. This creates recurring paid deliveries; subsequent eligible orders generally receive 5% off. It is not a free trial.
The discount appears at checkout, subject to product and brand exclusions. Future deliveries can be changed or canceled in your account. Check the final total and shipping; standard free shipping requires an eligible order over $49 after discounts and before tax. A store is listed in San Jose's Almaden area.
PetSmart official promotion and Autoship terms：https://www.petsmart.com/help/promotional-terms

PETCO：First Autoship delivery: 35% off, up to $20
First Autoship order · recurring paid deliveries
Set up Autoship for eligible products for the first time to receive 35% off the first order, up to $20. Subsequent eligible orders receive 5% off. Deliveries recur and are charged; change or cancel them in your account.
This is not a storewide coupon: exclusions apply to selected brands, prescription foods, litter and other products. Check the cart. First-order free shipping has separate spending and product conditions. An official store page lists Blossom Hill Road, San Jose.
Petco official Autoship help and first-order offer：https://www.petco.com/content/petco/PetcoStore/en_US/pet-services/help/autoship.html

COLD STONE CREAMERY：New members: buy one Creation, get one free
My Cold Stone Club welcome offer · check expiry
Join My Cold Stone Club and use the new-member BOGO Creation offer with the purchase of an eligible Creation. It is a buy-one-get-one offer, not a standalone free ice cream.
Registration also awards 25 points, which is not an immediate $5 credit. Check your account for expiry, sizes and store eligibility; a BOGO and a $5 points reward cannot be combined in one order. The San Jose Curtner Avenue store page also lists this welcome offer.
Cold Stone official welcome offer and FAQ：https://www.coldstonecreamery.com/mycsc/

CINNABON：New members: 4-count Original BonBites with a purchase
New-member welcome reward · 14 days after issue
Join Cinnabon Rewards as a new member, make a purchase and apply the welcome reward at checkout for a 4-count Original BonBites. Once per person; redeem within 14 days of issue.
The current offers page also lists a MiniBon option; follow the choices on your reward. Caramel Pecan and Chocolate BonBites are excluded. No offer stacking or third-party delivery; online orders may carry service fees. A store is listed at Eastridge, San Jose.
Cinnabon official new-member welcome terms：https://www.cinnabon.com/offers

AUNTIE ANNE'S：Unlock a pretzel offer with a purchase, then redeem with another item
New members must unlock offer · 45 days after receipt
Join Rewards and make a qualifying purchase of at least $1 to unlock the welcome offer. After receiving the reward, purchase one or more additional items and apply it at checkout to receive an eligible pretzel.
Choose Original, Cinnamon Sugar or Sweet Almond; single use within 45 days of receipt. No offer stacking or third-party delivery; taxes and online service fees are extra. A store is listed at Great Mall in Milpitas.
Auntie Anne's official welcome offer and purchase conditions：https://www.auntieannes.com/offers

AUNTIE ANNE'S：Birthday pretzel with qualifying spending in the previous year
Birthday reward valid 30 days · $1 spend in prior year
Spend at least $1 before taxes and fees through your Rewards account in the preceding 365 days to qualify. Redeem once through that account within 30 days of receiving the birthday offer.
Redeem for an Original, Sweet Almond or Cinnamon Sugar Pretzel. Prior spending is required; signing up alone does not qualify. No stacking or third-party delivery; taxes or online service fees may apply. Check the Great Mall location.
Auntie Anne's official birthday-offer conditions：https://www.auntieannes.com/offers

BAMPFA · BERKELEY：Nov 5: free gallery admission at BAMPFA
Thu Nov 5 · gallery opening hours
Gallery admission is free for everyone; film screenings require separate tickets.
BAMPFA’s November calendar lists Nov 5 as Free First Thursday. Pair the galleries with a downtown Berkeley walk; check gallery hours before leaving.
BAMPFA November 2026 calendar：https://bampfa.org/visit/calendar/2026-11

OMCA · OAKLAND：Nov 1: free galleries and special exhibitions at OMCA
Sun Nov 1 · derived from the first-Sunday rule
Free for everyone, including special exhibitions under the current policy. Advance booking is recommended; walk-up tickets are first come, first served.
Nov 1 is November’s first Sunday, calculated from the museum’s monthly policy. Food, shopping and parking cost extra; no membership is required.
OMCA free first Sundays and reservations：https://museumca.org/first-sundays/

ASIAN ART MUSEUM · SF：Nov 1: free general admission at the Asian Art Museum
Sun Nov 1 · 10 am–5 pm
General admission is free on the first Sunday; special exhibitions cost an additional $10. Booking a time slot is recommended.
The current monthly rule gives Nov 1. The museum is at 200 Larkin Street in San Francisco’s Civic Center; free general admission does not cover every exhibition.
Asian Art Museum ticketing：https://about.asianart.org/ticketing/

CONSERVATORY OF FLOWERS · SF：Nov 3: free admission to the Conservatory of Flowers
Tue Nov 3 · 10 am–4:30 pm; last entry 4 pm
General admission is free for everyone, regardless of residency. Check separate ticket requirements for special programs.
The official calendar confirms Nov 3, 2026. The Conservatory and Botanical Garden are separate venues; the Botanical Garden’s free day is Nov 10.
Official Conservatory free day on Nov 3：https://gggp.org/event/free-day-conservatory-of-flowers-13/

SAN JOSÉ MUSEUM OF ART：Nov 6: free evening at San José Museum of Art
Fri Nov 6 · 6–9 pm
Admission is free that evening. Register ahead for faster check-in; food, drinks and shopping cost extra.
The museum has published its November First Fridays page. Visit the downtown galleries after work and check the event page for entertainment updates.
SJMA November First Fridays：https://sjmusart.org/event/first-fridays-november-2026

COMPUTER HISTORY MUSEUM：Nov 7–8: eligible existing cardholders get free CHM admission
Nov 7–8 · derived from the first-full-weekend rule
An active Bank of America or Merrill card and matching photo ID cover one general admission for the cardholder only. Guests, special exhibitions and ticketed events are excluded.
The Mountain View museum’s current policy applies on each month’s first full weekend: Nov 7–8. Use an eligible card you already have.
CHM admission discounts and free-entry terms：https://computerhistory.org/plan-your-visit/discounts/

SAN FRANCISCO BOTANICAL GARDEN：Nov 10: free general admission to SF Botanical Garden
Tue Nov 10 · 7:30 am–5 pm; last entry 4 pm
General admission is free for everyone that day; paid classes and special events are excluded.
The official calendar confirms Nov 10. November’s last-entry time is earlier than October’s: arrive before 4 pm instead of assuming the October 5 pm cutoff.
Official Botanical Garden free day on Nov 10：https://gggp.org/event/free-day-san-francisco-botanical-garden-17/

MUSEUM OF THE AFRICAN DIASPORA · SF：Nov 14: free second-Saturday admission at MoAD
Sat Nov 14 · 11 am–5 pm, derived from the monthly rule
THRIVE @ MoAD offers free museum admission on the second Saturday each month. Check the day’s notice for programs and reservation requirements.
Nov 14 is November’s second Saturday. This listing confirms the current free-admission policy; it does not promise unannounced talks or performances.
MoAD visitor information and THRIVE policy：https://www.moadsf.org/visit

MUIR WOODS · NATIONAL PARK SERVICE：Nov 11: Muir Woods entrance-fee waiver for eligible visitors
Wed Nov 11 · check park hours
The 2026 entrance-fee waiver applies to U.S. citizens and residents only. Parking or shuttle reservations and their fees still apply.
Muir Woods’ official 2026 NPS list includes Veterans Day, Nov 11. Check eligibility and parking or shuttle availability before planning your redwood walk.
Muir Woods 2026 fee-free days and restrictions：https://www.nps.gov/muwo/planyourvisit/fees.htm

CHILI’S：Nov 11: Chili’s free select entrées for military and veterans
Wed Nov 11 · dine-in at participating locations
For active military and veterans only, from a select menu at participating restaurants, dine-in only. Beverages and gratuity are excluded; no substitutions or combining offers.
The official page explicitly dates the offer Nov 11, 2026. Ask your Bay Area restaurant about participation and accepted eligibility evidence; accompanying family members do not automatically eat free.
Chili’s 2026 Veterans Day terms：https://www.chilis.com/restaurant-events/veterans-day

WINCHESTER MYSTERY HOUSE · SAN JOSÉ：Santa Clara County residents: 25% off Winchester daytime tours
First 1,000 qualifying orders · check remaining availability
County residents use LOCALSFIRST for daytime Mansion Tours only, up to four tickets per order. Present photo ID with an eligible address on arrival; discounts cannot be combined.
The official resident discount is capped by order count, with no promise that availability lasts into November. Confirm the code still works at checkout before buying. Evening and special events are excluded.
Winchester county resident discount restrictions：https://winchestermysteryhouse.com/locals-discount/

LAKESHORE LEARNING：Oct 25–31: Halloween craft table at Lakeshore
Oct 25–31 · confirm daily craft hours with the store
The official 2026 store calendar lists a Trick-or-Treat craft week. Ask your nearby store about supplies, ages and attendance arrangements.
The activity features a Halloween creature craft. Do not assume the regular Saturday event hours apply throughout the week or treat retail promotions as free gifts.
Lakeshore 2026 in-store event calendar：https://img.lakeshorelearning.com/is/content/OCProduction/pdf/8597056_LE%20Year%20Calendar_2026_No%20Crop.pdf

Plan an early-November outing
Build a simple half-day around one free venue and a nearby activity.

Leave unannounced details open
As of Oct 5, some online Veterans Day and Black Friday content still points to 2025 or other countries. Listings use verified years, regions and eligibility; check later official announcements for changes.

title: Early November in the Bay Area: choose an area, then an event or free day
summary: Keep museum visits, crafts, nature outings and shopping simple: choose one main destination and one nearby stop, then check whether an offer is free, purchase-based or eligibility-limited.
keywords: Early November in the Bay Area: choose an area, then an event or free day
content:
Start with the November and region filters on the events page. Add the free filter if needed; free admission does not cover food, parking or separately ticketed activities.

Choose one main destination for your date

Find November events by date and area
Open the November filter, then narrow by culture, outdoors, food or family.
/this-month?when=november#monthly-events

Nov 1: compare OMCA and Asian Art Museum admission coverage, then choose one instead of rushing across the bay.
Nov 3–10: the Conservatory, BAMPFA, SJMA, Computer History Museum and Botanical Garden have different dates and eligibility; use the cards below.
Nov 11: Muir Woods’ entrance waiver does not cover parking reservations; Chili’s free entrée is limited to active military and veterans.
Nov 14: choose a Lowe’s store and an available Holiday Engine slot; MoAD’s free museum admission is another option.
Nov 15: check the list for confirmed nature or community programs. If weather cancels an outdoor activity, choose an indoor alternative in the same area.

Leave room in your plan
Decide your starting city, transport, group size and latest return time. Separate official event hours from travel estimates. Check missing opening hours before building a timed itinerary.

Find sights and resident resources city by city
The 101-city directory distinguishes in-city, nearby and cross-boundary places, helping you add a manageable nearby stop.
/guides/bay-area-101-city-exploration-living-guide

Verified November free days and conditional offers

Check eligibility and expiry first; reservations and remaining order quotas are not guaranteed.

BAMPFA · BERKELEY：Nov 5: free gallery admission at BAMPFA
Thu Nov 5 · gallery opening hours
Gallery admission is free for everyone; film screenings require separate tickets.
BAMPFA’s November calendar lists Nov 5 as Free First Thursday. Pair the galleries with a downtown Berkeley walk; check gallery hours before leaving.
BAMPFA November 2026 calendar：https://bampfa.org/visit/calendar/2026-11

OMCA · OAKLAND：Nov 1: free galleries and special exhibitions at OMCA
Sun Nov 1 · derived from the first-Sunday rule
Free for everyone, including special exhibitions under the current policy. Advance booking is recommended; walk-up tickets are first come, first served.
Nov 1 is November’s first Sunday, calculated from the museum’s monthly policy. Food, shopping and parking cost extra; no membership is required.
OMCA free first Sundays and reservations：https://museumca.org/first-sundays/

ASIAN ART MUSEUM · SF：Nov 1: free general admission at the Asian Art Museum
Sun Nov 1 · 10 am–5 pm
General admission is free on the first Sunday; special exhibitions cost an additional $10. Booking a time slot is recommended.

content:
At 2 am on Sunday Nov 1, clocks go back to 1 am. Phones usually adjust automatically; check manually set watches, car clocks and other devices. Specify Bay Area local time for cross-time-zone appointments.

Key dates and official services

California’s election is Nov 3, 2026, with polls open 7 am–8 pm. Regular online or postmarked voter registration is due Oct 19.
Eligible citizens who miss the regular deadline can conditionally register and vote at a county elections office, polling place or vote center; ballots are counted after verification.
Hand-delivered ballots are due by 8 pm Nov 3. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Nov 3 and received by the county elections office by Nov 10.

title: North Bay fall choices: markets, nature and culture through November 15
summary: Choose published October and November markets, stargazing, toddler storytime and exhibitions in the North Bay. Distinguish free programs from parking charges, adult-only sessions and separate museum campuses before adding a nearby walk.
keywords: North Bay fall choices: markets, nature and culture through November 15
content:
The North Bay is large. Choose one area—Marin, Napa Valley, Sonoma Valley or Solano—instead of packing several counties into a day. Start with one published activity, then add a local walk if weather and energy allow. These are not timed navigation routes; specific travel times have not been checked.

For produce and something to eat: choose one Saturday market

Healdsburg: Oct 10, 17, 24, 31 and Nov 7, 14, 8:30 am–noon. The new venue is Foley Family Community Pavilion at 3 North Street; the Tuesday season has ended. Shop and explore downtown without adding another cross-county event.
Sonoma Garden Park: the same six Saturdays, 9 am–1 pm, at 19996 7th Street East. Bring bags and expect harvest-dependent stock. This is not a Sonoma Plaza market; the addresses are different.
Food is purchased from vendors at both markets. The official pages do not list a separate admission charge; neither is a free-food offer.

For nature: choose a daytime talk or an evening star party

On Nov 8, Sugarloaf offers a colors, patterns and animal-signals talk outside the visitor center, 12:30–3:30 pm. Drop in during the session. The program is free with separate parking charges; it is a tabletop talk, not a mandatory three-hour hike.
The Nov 7 public star party runs 7–10 pm, with event tickets plus $10 parking per vehicle. Buy tickets and bring warm layers. Clouds affect viewing. Sips and Stars on Nov 13 is for ages 21+ and cannot substitute for a family star party.

For less favorable weather: toddler storytime and indoor art

Fairfax Library lists Spanish–English storytime for ages 0–5 on Nov 3 and 10. The 10:15 series lists an 11:45 end and also describes a 9:30 session. Attend only one and check that day’s listing; the full time block is not a promise of continuous performance.
Eames & Eames opens Oct 17 at The MAC, 607 St Helena Highway, with regular daily hours of 10 am–5 pm. General tickets are $25 for adults, $15 for ages 6–17 and free for ages 5 and under; check holidays and opening events separately. This is not the Yountville museum.
On Nov 15, Jack London Park’s author event discusses The Second Mrs. London from 2–3:30 pm; reserve ahead. There is no extra event fee, but entry costs $15 per vehicle. The second floor has stairs-only access; contact the park if step-free access is needed.

Solano fall walks: check access rules first

Dixon’s Lambtown and Rio Vista’s Bass Derby ended Oct 4. Consider the designated self-guided area at Jepson Prairie or Rio Vista’s riverfront afterward, but do not transfer spring vernal-pool bloom expectations to fall. Sandy Beach is not a swimming destination: swimming is prohibited and day-use construction or boat-ramp restrictions may change.

Dates: choose only the listed 2026 occurrences and check official pages again for weather or changes.
Costs: separate event admission, parking, meals and shopping; a free program does not make the whole trip cost-free.
Locations: distinguish The MAC from NVMY, Sonoma Garden Park from the plaza, and countywide studios from a downtown venue.
Group needs: decide around children’s ages, 21+ limits, stairs and return time before adding attractions.

title: November outdoors in the Peninsula and South Bay: marshes, redwoods or summit history
summary: Choose the November 2 El Corte de Madera hike, November 8 Mount Umunhum history walk or November 15 Ravenswood marsh outing by distance, stairs, meeting point and conditions. Free does not mean guided interpretation is available at any time.
keywords: November outdoors in the Peninsula and South Bay: marshes, redwoods or summit history
content:
Start with the hardest section, then the scenery

These outings are not interchangeable easy walks. Ravenswood is relatively level but still covers about three miles; El Corte de Madera is a multi-hour forest loop; Mount Umunhum has the shortest distance but many stairs. With children, older companions or limited recent exercise, compare the hardest section first. Photos and a family-friendly label are not enough, and meeting at the summit does not mean hiking there from the foothills.

Make one guided outing the day’s main activity

Monday, November 2: El Corte de Madera, 10 a.m.–1:30 p.m. For visitors comfortable with about four miles of forest trails and interested in old trees and sandstone.
Sunday, November 8: Mount Umunhum, 1–3 p.m. The focus is history; the roughly quarter-mile walk still includes 159 steps.
Sunday, November 15: Ravenswood, 9:30 a.m.–noon. About three miles of salt-marsh observation for families whose walking ability fits the outing.

The meeting point matters more than the preserve name

A preserve may have widely separated entrances. Save the event’s meeting point, then check the lot name and final approach. Skeggs Point is on Skyline Boulevard’s east side and prohibits a left turn from the north; this Ravenswood outing meets at the end of Bay Road; Mount Umunhum meets at summit parking. Do not accept the first result for the preserve name, and separately check whether the last leg is feasible by public transport.

Free outings still have participation procedures

Midpen’s guided outings are free and require a waiver at the meeting point. Follow event-specific booking instructions where required; no reservation button does not remove check-in. Groups of eight or more should contact staff first. Dogs may join only specifically labeled dog outings, and independent walks still follow each preserve’s own rules.

Shortening or canceling can be the right plan

A November listing cannot guarantee sunshine, bird sightings or dry trails. Heavy rain may cancel guided hikes and lighter rain may change the route; recheck event and closure notices. Bring water, layers and suitable shoes rather than relying on supplies in the hills. Ravenswood has no restrooms, so plan ahead. An easy meal afterward is a more flexible editorial suggestion than adding another distant long hike.

Check the correct 2026 date, meeting entrance and participation rules
Everyone can manage the distance, climbing or steps; age alone does not establish ability
Allow for transport, parking, meals and return time; a free guided outing is not an all-inclusive trip

Open the chosen event for registration and weather notices.

title: Autumn farmers’ markets in the Peninsula and South Bay: check moves and closures first
summary: Treat markets as practical weekly food stops: a Thursday evening in San Mateo or a South Bay Sunday morning, with confirmed October closures and a November relocation. Check purchases, parking, benefit rules and workshops separately before leaving.
keywords: Autumn farmers’ markets in the Peninsula and South Bay: check moves and closures first
content:
Shop where you will already be, instead of chasing four cities

For a first visit, list ingredients for two meals and one fruit or vegetable to try. Bring bags and a cooler bag for perishables. Compare quantity, ripeness and total price, and ask whether pricing is by weight or container. Budget food-truck meals separately from groceries to take home; an admission-free visit can still involve substantial purchases.

Four market directions and their exceptions

San Mateo: the officially listed November 5 session runs Thursday, 3–7 p.m., in the former Draeger’s lot at 222 East 4th Avenue, with produce and food trucks. It is different from the Saturday CSM campus market.
Mountain View: normally Sunday, 9 a.m.–1 p.m., at the Caltrain lot, 600 West Evelyn Avenue. November 8 moves to lots 4 and 8 at 190 Hope Street.
Campbell: normally Sunday, 9 a.m.–1 p.m., on East Campbell Avenue between Central Avenue and 3rd Street. It closes October 18, 2026 for Oktoberfest; festival stalls are not the usual farmers’ market operating as normal.
San Carlos: the operator lists a year-round Sunday market, 9 a.m.–1 p.m., but closes October 11, 2026 for the Art & Wine Faire. Recheck the exact street location and day’s notices.

On relocation days, separate the destination from parking

The November 8 Mountain View move frees the Caltrain lot for a 49ers home game. Market stalls occupying Hope Street parking areas do not make those spaces available to shoppers’ cars. Choose legal parking separately and check time limits, fees and closures. Transit passengers should save the dated market address and plan the walk instead of waiting at the usual entrance.

Ask the information booth about food benefits

Campbell’s operator lists EBT and WIC acceptance and an EBT fruit-and-vegetable match of up to $15. Ask the market information booth about payment, redemption and eligible purchases. It is not a cash gift for every visitor or a benefit for every hot-food stall. Rules differ between markets and programs, so do not apply one location’s limit everywhere.

For edible gifts, consider a structured preserving class

The November 14 Gifts from the Kitchen class in San Carlos requires separate UC registration; it is not a market add-on. It runs 9 a.m.–noon at 1839 Arroyo Avenue and costs $115 per person after September 30. Check availability, age suitability and allergy information before paying. Do not budget from an old early-bird heading or confuse untested home recipes with the course’s preserving methods.

Budget groceries, food eaten there, parking and transport separately
Ask vendors about allergens, quantities, payment and return terms
UVFM does not allow ordinary pets in food-stall areas; applicable service-animal rules are separate

Recheck temporary updates; year-round operations can still have exceptions.

title: East Bay nature programs in November: match the walk to your group
summary: Seven confirmed regional-park programs for November 1–15, with ages, meeting entrances, registration and difficulty. Choose separately between short family programs and 4.5–5.2-mile hill hikes.
keywords: East Bay nature programs in November: match the walk to your group
content:
This is a selection, not a one-day itinerary. Programs span Oakley, Antioch, the Livermore area, Hayward, Martinez and Fremont. Choose one main activity and arrange travel and lunch from your own starting point.

For children, check distance as well as age

For ages 5+, Big Break offers a one-hour walk of about 0.5–2 miles with an adult. Coyote Hills has a one-hour parent-and-child birding program on November 14.
Hayward’s November 15 morning session is ages 6+, requires registration and lends binoculars; heavy rain cancels. Other sessions’ all-ages labels do not apply.
Monday birding in Hayward and Martinez lists 2–5-mile routes. All-ages eligibility does not guarantee suitability for a young child’s stamina.

For hill hikes, check terrain before price

On November 1, Brushy Peak is about 4.5 miles with 501–1,000 feet of climbing, ages 7+ with an adult. Black Diamond is about 5.2 miles with 1,300 feet of climbing, ages 12+. Both registration windows run October 6 at 9 am through October 28 at 4 pm. Obtain confirmation before arranging transport; bring suitable shoes, water and stamina.

Check each program: time, meeting point and registration

Big Break nature walks: four November dates
November 1, 8, 14 and 15, 2–3 pm. Free program and parking; no registration. Explore Delta wetlands with a naturalist. Ages 5+ with adult participation; routes are approximately 0.5–2 miles, mainly paved and generally level.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/big-break-nature-walk-29

Black Diamond Trails Challenge: a 5.2-mile hill hike
November 1, 9 am–1 pm. Free program; $5 parking when kiosk staffed; registration required. A loop for ages 12+ with about 1,300 feet of climbing, steep slopes and uneven dirt trails. Suitable for hikers comfortable with substantial hill walks.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/black-diamond-trails-challenge-hike

Brushy Peak: Indigenous heritage and a hill hike
November 1, 9 am–1 pm. Free program; advance registration required. Walk a roughly 4.5-mile loop north of Livermore while learning Indigenous history and ecology. Ages 7+ with adult participation; 501–1,000 feet of climbing and steep sections.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/native-american-heritage-month-brushy-peak-hike-1

Monday birding at Hayward: West Winton entrance
November 2, 9 am–noon. Free; no registration. Watch seasonal shoreline birds on a gravel route listed at 2–5 miles. This session meets at West Winton Avenue, not the Grant Avenue entrance used on November 15.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/monday-birding-hayward-regional-shoreline

Monday shoreline birding in Martinez
November 9, 9 am–noon. Free; no registration. Watch seasonal birds near the marina. The all-ages listing describes a 2–5-mile gravel route with 0–500 feet of elevation change; consider children’s stamina.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/monday-birding-radke-martinez-shoreline

Birding basics for kids at Coyote Hills
November 14, 11 am–noon. Free drop-in program; $5 standard vehicle parking. Learn about birds through games and observation. The description specifies ages 5+ with a parent participating. After the hour-long program, decide whether to explore further.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/birding-basics-kids

Bay Bird Mornings in Hayward: ages 6+
November 15, 8–10 am. Free; registration required, subject to availability. Beginners are welcome and binoculars are available to borrow. Ages 6+; meet at the Grant Avenue entrance. Heavy rain cancels.
https://www.ebparks.org/events/bay-bird-mornings-hayward-0

Hayward has two different meeting entrances
Use West Winton Avenue on November 2 and Grant Avenue on November 15. Navigate to the stated meeting point rather than just a park name. Big Break’s algae alerts concern water; shoreline activities do not authorize water access.

Check ages, adult participation, registration status and meeting point.
Separate programs from parking: standard parking is $5 at Coyote Hills and $5 at Black Diamond when the kiosk is staffed.
Bring water, a wind layer and walking shoes; use confirmation messages for cancellations or rescheduling.

title: San Francisco fall markets: tastings, produce and the season finale
summary: Four confirmed dates cover baking demonstrations, fall-fruit samples, Mission festivities and the final market. Distinguish free programs from paid food and find the right tent.
keywords: San Francisco fall markets: tastings, produce and the season finale
content:
Treat a market as a relaxed half-day: choose a program, then leave time for shopping and a break. The four entries are on different dates, not a same-day route, and samples are not a lunch plan.

Four dates with different highlights

Seasonal baking demonstration with Flour Craft
October 10, 11–11:45 am. Free demonstration; books and market purchases cost extra. Heather Hardcastle demonstrates seasonal baking in front of the Ferry Building, followed by a cookbook signing. Samples do not constitute a free meal.
https://foodwise.org/events/heather-hardcastle-the-flour-craft-bakery-cafe-cookbook/

Día de los Muertos and Halloween at Mission Community Market
October 29, 3–7 pm. Free community activities; vendor food and shopping cost extra. An after-school market with crafts, costumes and seasonal food activities; DJ Lamont plays 5–7 pm. Vendor foods such as pan dulce and mole are sold separately.
https://foodwise.org/events/dia-de-los-muertos-and-halloween-at-mission-community-market/

Fall fruit tasting and Mexican baking at Ferry Plaza
October 31, 11 am–1 pm; demonstration 11–11:45 am. Free activities and samples; market purchases cost extra. Taste fall fruit, collect recipes and vote for favorites at the orange tent. Sofía Jiménez of Tutuli demonstrates baking at the green Classroom tent at 11 am.
https://foodwise.org/events/fall-fruit-celebration/

Mission Community Market: final day of the 2026 season
November 12, 3–7 pm. Browse the market; produce, food and goods cost extra. Foodwise confirms November 12 as the last market of 2026, with a planned return in March 2027. Shop for seasonal produce; extra performances or free meals have not been announced.
https://foodwise.org/events/mission-community-market-last-day-of-the-season/

Green tent for demonstrations, orange for fall-fruit samples

The green Foodwise Classroom tent is directly in front of the Ferry Building. On October 31, the orange Seasonal Spotlight tent hosts fruit activities from 11 am–1 pm; the Tutuli demonstration is 11–11:45 am in the green tent.

Mission’s market street and final date

Current visitor information places the market on 22nd Street between Mission and Valencia, while the footer retains 84 Bartlett. Follow current directions and signs. November 12, 3–7 pm is the confirmed 2026 finale; do not continue applying the Thursday schedule afterward.

Only listed demonstrations, crafts or samples are free; meals, goods and cookbooks cost extra.
Bring a shopping bag, water and your chosen budget; ask about ingredients for food allergies.
Recheck programs, vendors and weather; archival photos do not guarantee current stock.

title: Useful Bay Area apps and websites: rides, food, housing, savings and local life
summary: A practical directory of Bay Area rides, transit, parking, Chinese food delivery, groceries, housing, savings, secondhand exchanges, events and public resources, with official links, setup tips, coverage and limits for visitors, newcomers and established residents.
keywords: Useful Bay Area apps and websites: rides, food, housing, savings and local life
content:
Treat your phone as a practical toolkit. Start with what you will use this week, then add services for your address, commute and interests. Choose ride, delivery and membership services as needed. The directory includes websites so you can look things up before installing an app.

Choose a starting set for your situation

Visitors: a map, Uber or Lyft, transit payment that fits your route, and one food or event service. Check the airport’s official pickup instructions before requesting a ride.
Newcomers: add housing search such as Zillow or Redfin, a grocery service that reaches your address, a deal source such as Dealmoon, and your own library and municipal websites.
Established residents: assess memberships against actual spending, use Meetup for recurring interests, try library resources before adding subscriptions, and configure fire, air-quality or earthquake notifications as relevant.
For Chinese-language needs: compare HungryPanda, Fantuan, Weee! and Dealmoon, checking the address, merchants, delivery method and account region for each.

Apps, memberships and coverage are separate
An available download does not establish coverage or free access. Some features may require the app even when a website is available. “Primarily web” describes the suggested route, not the absence of other products. Follow official download links and check the developer.

Browse the directory by everyday task

Useful Bay Area app and platform directory

Search names or tasks and expand a card for practical steps and limits. Official links open the service or its download information; this site does not download apps or create accounts for you.

Platform: Google Maps | google-maps
Compare driving, transit, walking and cycling routes, and save hotel and attraction entrances.
For: For first-time Bay Area visitors traveling between neighborhoods or cities in one day.
How: Enter the specific entrance, set your departure or arrival date and time, and compare transfers and walking sections. Check the return trip separately.
Coverage: Maps and routes cover the Bay Area; transit information depends on data supplied by local operators.
Check: Offline maps do not provide transit, walking or cycling directions. Check the operator's notices for live arrivals and service disruptions.
https://www.google.com/maps/about/
Google Maps: Official Maps product entry point, with access to mapping, navigation and saved places.
https://www.google.com/maps/about/
Google Maps Help — Get directions: Supports multiple travel modes and directions based on departure or arrival date and time.
https://support.google.com/maps/answer/144339?hl=en
Google Maps Help — Offline maps: Offline mode does not provide transit, walking or cycling directions, or live traffic.
https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6291838?hl=en-in
511 Open Data: Bay Area transportation data is supplied to mapping and travel applications, including Google, Apple and Transit.
https://511.org/open-data

Look up routes, transit arrivals and places on Apple devices, with a web entry point also available.
For: For visitors using an iPhone and new residents saving everyday destinations.
How: Confirm the destination entrance, then select transit or driving. Save your accommodation and stations, and check route alerts before leaving.
Coverage: Apple lists San Francisco among its detailed city maps; Bay Area transit information varies by route and live data availability.
Check: Web and native-app features differ. Check Apple's documentation for supported browsers, languages and regional features.

Apple Maps: The official entry point describes detailed San Francisco maps, directions and live transit information where available.
https://www.apple.com/maps/

Platform: Transit | transit-app
See nearby bus, train and ferry arrivals together with step-by-step transfer directions.
For: For people transferring between operators who want to switch between fewer apps.
How: Select your direction and travel date, check nearby stops and service alerts, and use step-by-step navigation for complex trips.
Coverage: Its official Bay Area directory includes Muni, BART, Caltrain, AC Transit, VTA, SMART and ferry services.
Check: Arrival times are predictions. Some full schedules and extended features require Royale; check what is free or sponsored by your agency.
https://transitapp.com/en/region/sf-bay-area
Transit — SF Bay Area: Lists supported Bay Area operators and provides app downloads, trip planning, arrivals and service alerts.
https://transitapp.com/en/region/sf-bay-area

https://help.transitapp.com/article/362-royale-faq

Platform: Clipper | clipper
Manage Bay Area transit-card balances and passes, and add a transit card to your mobile wallet.
For: For travel across buses, rail and ferries, or for managing a discounted transit card.
How: Register your card and follow the instructions to add it to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. Before entering, confirm the card is ready on your device and funded.
Coverage: Available on participating Bay Area operators; confirm discounts and tap-on/tap-off rules for each service.
Check: Registering a plastic card alone does not enable phone tapping. Transferring it to a wallet deactivates the plastic card for transit. MuniMobile no longer sells single-ride tickets, but some passes remain.
https://www.clippercard.com/clipper-on-your-phone.html
Clipper — Clipper on Your Phone: Explains app-based account management, mobile wallets, card transfers and deactivation of the plastic card for transit.
https://www.clippercard.com/clipper-on-your-phone.html
SFMTA — MuniMobile: Single-ride ticket sales ended September 1, 2026. Some other fare products remain on sale in 2026; the full transition is not yet complete.
https://www.sfmta.com/getting-around/muni/fares/munimobile
2026-10-02

Platform: BART Official | bart-official
Check BART routes, live trains and service alerts, and manage station parking.
For: For BART commuters, airport transfers and riders parking at a station.
How: Choose your origin and destination and check the last train and elevator alerts. For parking, open the parking feature and verify your plate, station and parking product.
Coverage: Covers the BART system; check the relevant operator separately for connecting Muni, Caltrain or bus services.
