title: An autumn walk at Sunset Dunes: start at Noriega and leave time for the coast
summary: Choose a manageable stretch of Sunset Dunes for public art, rest stops, and ocean views. This October afternoon plan works on ordinary days as well as weekends.
keywords: An autumn walk at Sunset Dunes: start at Noriega and leave time for the coast
content:
Sunset Dunes runs between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard, with public art, recreation spaces, and ocean-view seating listed by the city. A temporary restroom is at Noriega. Treat the ocean as a backdrop for a relaxed walk; the two-mile length is not a required route, and performances are not guaranteed every day in October.

Editorial plan: a flexible 90-minute afternoon

Meet where Noriega Street reaches the oceanfront park. Find the restroom and return route before choosing north or south.
Pause after 20–30 minutes to choose a favorite artwork or watch the ocean from a seat. With children, separate active riding from quiet observation.
Leave a buffer before returning to the starting point. For sunset, check that day's time and return transport; choose a meal stop along the way home.

October preparation: let the wind guide your visit
Bring a windproof layer and water. Share the route with cyclists and keep photo stops out of the through path. Dunes and the beach are not shortcuts. Check current access and registration for new facilities or community classes.

title: An hour in San Mateo's Japanese Garden: koi, bamboo, and the Central Park construction update
summary: Plan the Japanese Garden before or after lunch for its pond, stone pagoda, and bamboo. Current playground and picnic-area construction changes what families can use.
keywords: An hour in San Mateo's Japanese Garden: koi, bamboo, and the Central Park construction update
content:
The Japanese Garden is inside Central Park at 50 East 5th Avenue. City hours are 10 am–4 pm Monday–Friday and 11 am–4 pm on weekends; dogs are not allowed in the garden. Features include a koi pond, granite pagoda, teahouse, and bamboo. This October plan does not promise cherry blossoms or a fish-feeding demonstration.

Editorial plan: an hour around lunch

On weekends, meet after 11 am and read entrance notices first. If early, stay in the outer areas open that day.
Observe the pond, then compare textures in the bamboo and stone pagoda. Ask children to find three shades of green without running, climbing, or feeding fish.
Eat downtown after the walk. Leave room for rest or the journey home instead of adding another distant attraction.

Construction update: tentative reopening later in October
The city’s September update says the playground boardwalk is being installed and other major improvements are complete. Reopening is tentatively expected later in October 2026, with no specific date announced. The park overview still lists playground and picnic-area closures during construction. Check the project notice and barriers before planning play equipment or picnic use; a tentative date does not mean the area is open.

title: Begin birdwatching at Alviso Marina without committing to a salt-pond loop
summary: Spend an hour noticing salt ponds, wetlands, and birds at Alviso. Choose a short county-park visit separately from longer refuge trails, with intermittent closure information.
keywords: Begin birdwatching at Alviso Marina without committing to a salt-pond loop
content:
The county park entrance is at 1195 Hope Street, with regular hours of 8 am to sunset. It adjoins Don Edwards National Wildlife Refuge, whose boundaries and rules differ. Fall offers migrating-bird observations, but sightings depend on tides, weather, and the day.

Editorial plan: three observation tasks in one hour

Read the map at the county park entrance and choose a short open route and return point; skip the pressure to complete a levee loop.
Stop at a designated viewing spot and notice whether a bird is wading, swimming, or flying. Share binoculars and record behavior instead of chasing a species count.
Save half your energy for the return. Turn back at barriers, strong wind, or fatigue and compare notes at the parking area.

Check construction and dog access first
County notices list intermittent hauling-related closures on Mallard Slough and eastern Alviso Slough. Follow current barriers even when an older map shows a connection. Most refuge trails prohibit dogs; county-park pet rules do not automatically extend onto salt-pond levees.

Editorial plan: choose a two-hour version by interest

Saturday short version: animals, the hay barn, and farm tools, plus any listed naturalist program. Avoid promising children a train ride.

Let children choose a tool or crop, guess its use, then check the interpretation. Finish with a quiet moment to compare discoveries.

Separate parking from admission and check event pricing
Parking is listed as free, but admission is charged and the entrance is cashless. Special events can change prices and activities, so check your date. Dogs, bicycles, and modern recreation equipment such as balls are prohibited; focus on the farm visit.

title: A free cultural visit in Richmond: factories and families at the Rosie visitor center
summary: Explore everyday Bay Area life during World War II at the Rosie the Riveter Visitor Education Center. Clear admission and parking information makes this a practical October half-day.

content:
The Visitor Education Center is at 1414 Harbour Way South, Suite 3000, with regular daily hours of 10 am–5 pm and free admission and parking listed by NPS. Exhibits and films explore factory work, family, and community life. A first visit need not cover every historic site in Richmond.

Editorial plan: start with a person's story, then a city's

Allow about an hour for exhibits. Choose a person or everyday object and discuss how wartime changed work, migration, and family roles.
Check film times on arrival and choose one suited to your group. With children, ask about running time before committing.
If the weather suits, take a short walk in the open waterfront area outside, then return to the same parking point. On a rainy day, the center alone is enough.

Free center admission does not cover every nearby attraction

Meet near 300 N. Court Street, confirm the parking area's closing time and restroom location, and use the official short-loop map.
Observe the wetlands along open Killdeer and Duck Pond sections, using two stops for birdwatching. Turn back if the surface does not suit your stroller.
Plan your return before the parking area closes and rest at the starting point. Avoid an unplanned extension to another entrance just because trails connect.

title: A Pleasanton Saturday: shop for two meals, then visit the free local museum
summary: Combine downtown Pleasanton's Saturday market and Museum on Main in one easy morning. Visit the museum before buying chilled food, then head home.
keywords: A Pleasanton Saturday: shop for two meals, then visit the free local museum
content:
PCFMA's Pleasanton market is at 46 W Angela Street on Saturdays year-round, 9 am–1 pm. Museum on Main is at 603 Main Street, normally free Tuesday–Saturday, 10 am–4 pm, and closed on major holidays. October 2026 Saturdays fall on the 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th, and 31st; these are calendar-based regular visit options, not five special events.

Editorial plan: browse first and shop last

Around 9:30 am, browse and note what you want before filling bags. Choose a specific intersection for meeting friends.
After 10 am, visit the museum for Pleasanton history. Give one topic 30–45 minutes before deciding to stay longer.

title: Bay Area street parking: read the signs before paying
summary: Use a simple pre-parking routine and the correct official resources for San Francisco, Oakland, San Jose, and San Mateo, without assuming one city’s free periods apply throughout the Bay Area.
keywords: Bay Area street parking: read the signs before paying
content:
Parking mistakes often begin with paying for an empty space before noticing another sign. There is no universal Bay Area free-parking schedule: rules can differ by block, side of the road, and event date even within one city. Confirm how long you may stay before paying. For longer visits, locating a garage with suitable vehicle access can save repeated circling.

Step 1: read the full set of signs

Walk along the space to inspect signs in both directions. Read the arrows, days, hours, maximum stay, and permit exceptions, then check sweeping, loading, commute tow-away, and temporary construction signs. Use the local date and include the next day for an overnight stay. An unpainted curb does not automatically permit parking; intersections, sidewalks, driveways, and hydrants have separate restrictions.

Step 2: check the city and date, not neighboring rules

In San Francisco, also check SFMTA’s daylighting guidance: generally leave 20 feet clear on the vehicle approach side of a marked or unmarked crosswalk, or 15 feet where there is a curb extension. Red curbs or no-parking signs may define a different distance. On a two-way street, check the right-hand approach in the direction of travel; on a one-way street, check both curbside approaches.

San Francisco: check meters, sweeping, and residential permits separately. SFMTA permits parking after the sweeper has actually cleaned the curbside, while other restrictions remain; a clean-looking road does not prove sweeping occurred.
Oakland: use the official sweeping map for the block and the relevant year’s holiday list; do not simply apply San Francisco’s sweeping practice.
San Jose: read maximum stays on the meter and signs. For longer visits, check each ParkSJ garage’s entrance, access hours, and current charges.
San Mateo: downtown has different parking zones. Check streets, garages, and private lots separately rather than treating the Peninsula as a single pricing area.

Step 3: a successful payment does not extend the legal stay

Check whether payment requires a plate, space number, or location code, then select a duration and save confirmation. A mobile extension does not override the maximum stay or a no-parking period. If payment fails, check the city’s malfunction guidance or move rather than assuming parking is free. San Francisco explicitly does not accept meter payments by QR code; verify other cities’ mobile methods through their own official sites.

Finally: record your return time and a backup garage

Save the full sign set and parking location; check today’s and tomorrow’s restrictions.
Confirm the payment matches your vehicle or space and set an early return reminder.
Check garage entrances, height clearance, vehicle retrieval hours, and event-day pricing.
If plans run late, check whether you may remain instead of assuming payment allows unlimited extensions.

title: Using FasTrak: separate bridge tolls, express lanes, and rental cars
summary: Distinguish bridge tolls from optional express lanes, arrange payment for your own or a rental vehicle, check carpool requirements, and recognize fraudulent payment texts.
keywords: Using FasTrak: separate bridge tolls, express lanes, and rental cars
content:
Seeing FasTrak in navigation does not mean the entire freeway is tolled or that an account automatically grants carpool discounts. Separate which bridge you will cross from whether you choose an express lane, then check the vehicle and payment method. Rental toll services may cover bridges without covering express lanes; ask at pickup rather than untangling charges later.

First distinguish bridge tolls from optional express lanes

Bridges: check the named bridge, direction, and vehicle category. The Golden Gate Bridge charges southbound into San Francisco and does not take cash at the bridge. Use FasTrak’s bridge directory for other crossings.
Express lanes: general-purpose lanes remain an option. Read destinations, current tolls, and operating periods before entering, and use permitted lane markings; do not cross double white lines to reach an exit.
The two toll types are separate. Do not add the prices for different destinations on one toll sign, and do not apply express lane carpool discounts directly to bridges.

Account, tag, and carpool eligibility are separate checks

Regular or short-term license plate accounts can pay bridge tolls but do not provide express lane access. Before using an express lane, confirm a valid FasTrak account and suitable tag; carpool discounts require a correctly set Flex. Occupancy rules vary: when checked, two-person carpools were free on I-580, while ordinary two-person vehicles paid half price on US-101, subject to tag requirements. For bridges, separately check occupancy, hours, designated lanes, and tags; six state-owned bridges changed their requirements in 2026.

Check vehicle registration and rental-plan coverage

For your own car, check account status, the plate and issuing state, and mount the tag as instructed. Ask a rental company whether its plan covers bridges and express lanes, what service fees apply, and how to opt out if paying yourself. With your own FasTrak, register the rental plate and accurate start and end dates, update extensions, and remove the tag on return. For bridge-only trips, check short-term plate options and deadlines. Pay an existing invoice through the invoice-payment route; opening an account is not a substitute.

Check before driving and verify notices independently

FasTrak explicitly does not request payment through texts with website links. If a message says payment is due today, manually open bayareafastrak.org to check records or contact official support, rather than entering payment details through the text. Compare travel dates, the bridge or lane, and your rental period; use the official inquiry route for discrepancies.

List toll bridges separately from any express lanes you may use.
Check operating periods and occupancy rules for your date; do not assume all weekends are free.
Before driving, confirm plate registration, tag mounting, and the correct occupancy setting.
For rentals, confirm coverage, service fees, and the registration end date.

A move-out clearout gets complicated when a sofa, old computer and leftover paint are treated as one load. List the items, then find each service. County household hazardous waste programs differ from city bulky pickup, and a neighbor's included pickups may not apply to your account.

Sort into three categories before booking transport

San Francisco: Recology bulky pickup eligibility depends on an active residential account and housing type. Hazardous waste uses a separate HHW service.
Peninsula: book San Mateo County HHW in advance. Confirm furniture pickup with your city's hauler.
South Bay: Santa Clara County HHW requires appointments and residency checks. Palo Alto residents use the city program.
East Bay: Alameda County residents can find facilities through StopWaste. Permanent facilities do not require appointments, but check opening dates and accepted items. Other counties have their own programs.
North Bay: start with Marin HHW, while Novato has its own facility. Marin eligibility does not extend to Sonoma or Napa.

Confirm acceptance before moving items

Photograph items and note quantities and approximate dimensions, then ask about acceptance and fees. Resident programs generally cover waste from your own household; business, contractor and collected waste need separate checks. Some drop-off addresses arrive only after booking, so use your confirmation for directions. Do not rely on an old map or assume one disposal fee covers every item.

title: Who to contact in the Bay Area: 311 reports, 211 referrals and emergency help
summary: Separate city infrastructure reports from community support, find San Francisco, San José, Oakland and county contacts, and write a useful service request.
keywords: Who to contact in the Bay Area: 311 reports, 211 referrals and emergency help
content:
A broken streetlight, a need for food assistance and a sudden injury call for different services. First assess immediate danger, then identify the city and county where the issue occurs. Your home address does not necessarily determine the responsible agency. A clear description reduces transfers and helps you track the outcome.

Choose the right kind of help

911: contact emergency services immediately for fire, a serious medical emergency or immediate danger to a person. Do not wait for a web service request.
311: city information and infrastructure issues such as potholes, streetlights, graffiti and illegal dumping. Accepted categories depend on the city and location.
211: non-emergency referrals for food, housing, bills and family support. The consultation is free; the referred program may have fees, eligibility rules or limited capacity.

Report by city and find support by county

San Francisco: use SF311. Call 311 within the city, check the official full number from outside it, or find services through SF.gov.
San José: select the current issue category on the San José 311 website or app and save the receipt and tracking number.
Oakland: use the OAK311 website for ordinary issues. Follow its telephone instructions for active infrastructure problems such as flooding or fallen trees; call 911 if someone faces immediate danger.
Counties: search 211 Bay Area or the county provider by city or ZIP code. Telephone, text and online response hours may differ; state the language you need.
Do not assume 311 works in every city. Find Report a problem or Public Works on the city website. If a three-digit number fails, use the official full number or website.

Make the report easy to locate and follow up

Include the issue address, nearest intersection, side of the street, observation time and practical impact. From a safe position, photograph only the visible public facility or issue, avoiding faces, belongings inside vehicles and private documents. Keep identity documents, account details and medical information out of public descriptions; use designated official fields for contact details. Save the reference and add changes to that record rather than duplicating it. A referral to another team still needs follow-up.

A city service request template
The issue is at [city/address or intersection/side of street]. At [date and time], I observed [specific problem], affecting [walking/lighting/other]. The photo shows [public facility or issue]. Please confirm whether your department handles this; if a referral is needed, please provide the correct contact and follow-up method.

For 211, begin with your county or ZIP code, the most urgent need and your language. After a referral, confirm appointments, documents, costs and waiting times with the actual provider.

Distinguish emergency danger, a city service request and community assistance.
Verify the issue location and the service’s coverage.
Keep sensitive personal information out of public text and photos.
Save the reference or referral provider and plan a follow-up.

title: San Francisco schools: from address checks to SFUSD enrollment
summary: Use your actual address, your child's grade and intended school year to find the right SFUSD process, understand school assignments, and explore CCSF and San Francisco State separately.
keywords: San Francisco schools: from address checks to SFUSD enrollment
content:
Start with three questions: where you actually live, your child's grade, and the intended school year. Save official links before comparing programs and travel arrangements, so a property's mention of a nearby school is not mistaken for an admission promise. This guide focuses on public K–12; colleges follow separate admissions processes.

Check the address and understand application-based assignment

Open School Finder from the SFUSD school directory, search with the actual street address and grade, then confirm residency eligibility and the relevant program with the Enrollment Center. Mailing cities, ZIP codes and property listings do not replace verification. SFUSD assigns schools after application using its rules and available seats; neither proximity nor an elementary attendance area reserves a seat. Check TK, elementary, middle and high school rules separately. An elementary placement does not establish the entire pathway through high school; elsewhere in the Bay Area, different districts may serve different grade levels.

Follow the process for the school year and student status

New students seeking 2026–27 enrollment can contact the Enrollment Center throughout the year. Use ParentVUE from the Apply page or the official paper/PDF process, then confirm the school, grade and start date.
For 2027–28, choose the next-year application and check its opening date and deadline. Distinguish the current school year, application receipt and final assignment.
Check residency, age and other documents against the official list and submit them only through official channels, not this site or public groups. Ask the Enrollment Center for help with missing documents, temporary housing or language support.

Current students seeking another school should check the applicable transfer process. Spring Transfer serves eligible current SFUSD students and excludes charter-school students. A successful assignment automatically replaces the previous placement; it is not an exploratory request that you can accept or decline later. For attendance across district boundaries, check interdistrict permits with both the district of residence and the receiving district.

Use visits to compare everyday needs

Shortlist two or three schools from the official directory and check tour bookings. Ask about language programs, learning support, school hours, after-school availability and transport; try the journey in advance. A visit does not promise admission, and access to classrooms or school activities requires permission. Check program requirements for the intended year.

Universities and community colleges: separate campus and admission checks

CCSF's location directory includes Ocean Campus and centers such as Mission and Chinatown/North Beach; the class schedule determines where a course meets. Start degree, certificate or transfer study through Start Here, then follow the class-registration instructions. At San Francisco State, choose the appropriate applicant type in Admissions and use Visit Campus for bookings or self-guided maps. Both are separate from K–12 district assignment: living nearby does not replace an application. Confirm visit dates, accessible facilities and permitted areas with the institution.

A checklist message for the enrollment office
I need enrollment for [school year], [grade], as a [new student / current student transferring schools / interdistrict applicant], starting in [month]. Please confirm the correct application, address verification, documents, assignment and registration steps, and contacts for [language / learning support]. I will provide the full address and documents only through the designated official channel.

Record the grade, school year and intended start month separately.
Confirm the address and application type with the district.
Save the receipt and confirm the final school and registration requirements.
Check transport, after-school care and tour bookings.

Select the school year before opening the relevant system or contacting the Enrollment Center.

title: Peninsula schools and districts: check address and grade before enrolling
summary: Distinguish elementary, high-school, and unified districts; check the right school year before arranging enrollment, transfers, language support, and college visits.
keywords: Peninsula schools and districts: check address and grade before enrolling
content:
Start with the intended school year, grade, and actual residential address. A listing labeled San Mateo, Redwood City, or Palo Alto does not establish a school district or assigned school. This guide begins with public K–12 district lookup; private schools and specialized programs have separate application rules.

Start with the county directory, then check elementary and high-school districts

San Mateo County: use the SMCOE directory to identify the district serving the address. The county includes unified districts and separate elementary and high-school districts; siblings in different grades may need two offices.
For the San Mateo–Foster City area, check elementary or middle school through the SMFCSD locator and separately check SMUHSD for high school. A locator result does not guarantee space, and this district pairing does not apply throughout the Peninsula.
Palo Alto: use School Finder on the PAUSD registration page for the residential address and intended grade. A mailing-city name, nearby school, or property advertisement cannot replace official confirmation.

Handle enrollment, transfers, and language support separately

After selecting the school year, use the district checklist for residence, age, health, and other documents, submit through its system, and save the receipt. Moving during the current year differs from next-year priority enrollment; an old deadline does not establish whether you can apply. SMUHSD confirms placement after staff review, and SMFCSD may assign another school based on grade-level capacity. Ask about the separate forms, review, and notification processes for intradistrict and interdistrict transfers; submitting a form is not approval.

If English is not the main home language, ask about the home-language survey, assessment, interpretation, and classroom support; PAUSD provides an English learner services entry point. For an existing learning-support plan, ask how to transfer it securely and arrange continuity. Also discuss adjustment and after-school care without assuming every school offers the same programs.

Ask about daily school life; use separate systems for college

Use the official directory to reach school websites and arrange an office appointment, information session, or open house. Compare classes, bell times, pickup arrangements, and after-school availability and costs. For College of San Mateo, find maps and visits on the homepage and apply through Apply. At Stanford, use Engage for visits and Apply for first-year or transfer requirements. Colleges do not assign admission through K–12 residential boundaries, and visiting does not guarantee acceptance.

Enter addresses only through official channels
Enter your full residential address in the official locator. Do not post a child’s name, date of birth, home address, or documents in public questions, community posts, or this website. Ask the district about alternative verification and assistance if documents are missing or you share housing or have temporary accommodation.

A short district inquiry template
Hello, we plan to apply for [grade] in [school year/month] and have checked your official address locator. Should we use new-student enrollment, an intradistrict school change, or an interdistrict transfer? What documents are needed, and how do we confirm school placement and the start date? We would also like information about [language/learning/after-school care] support.

Save official lookup results for the grade, school year, and district.
Confirm review completion, school placement, and the first attendance date.
Ask about language support, transportation, and after-school care.
Arrange college visits and applications separately from K–12 enrollment.

title: South Bay schools and districts: navigating San José, Cupertino, and Sunnyvale
summary: Use Santa Clara County’s official directory to distinguish unified districts from separate elementary and high-school districts, including school-year boundary changes.
keywords: South Bay schools and districts: navigating San José, Cupertino, and Sunnyvale
content:
A South Bay city can contain several school districts, and one address may have separate elementary and high-school districts. Establish the grade, school year, and actual residence, then use Santa Clara County Office of Education lookup and directory tools. County tools help identify the district; the district confirms the school and placement.

Check address and grade in all three cities

San José: the city name does not automatically mean SJUSD. Once district residence is confirmed, use the 2026–27 locator for that year and the separate locator for 2027–28 onward; future boundaries do not establish current placement.
Cupertino: Cupertino Union’s (CUSD) elementary-level locator does not replace a high-school lookup. For high school, separately use Fremont Union High School District’s (FUHSD) Address Check Tool.
Sunnyvale: Sunnyvale School District enrollment and FUHSD high-school enrollment are separate, but not every Sunnyvale address belongs to these districts. Cross-check the county directory and the relevant district tools first.

Follow up on placement after submitting

Prepare the documents listed for the correct school year, submit online or request in-person help, and save the receipt. SJUSD states that enrollment is complete only after requirements are met and staff send confirmation; ask other districts about review status, assigned school, and attendance arrangements too. Interdistrict and intradistrict transfers have their own processes, so ask about release, acceptance, and waiting lists. Do not assume finishing middle school automatically completes high-school enrollment.

Newcomer families can ask about English learner assessment, interpretation, counselor meetings, and secure transfer of prior records and learning-support plans. For a midyear move, confirm course continuity, especially high-school credits and schedules. Ask both schools to explain the transition before assuming the receiving arrangements are complete.

Arrange school visits and college exploration through official sites

Open school websites through the SCCOE directory and ask the office about available visits. Focus on courses, after-school capacity and fees, daily transportation, and a contact for new students. SJSU has separate admissions and campus-visit resources. At Foothill College, review application steps, then locate the office and campus map. College applications depend on student type, term, and program; K–12 residential assignment does not apply, and visiting does not reserve admission.

Enter addresses only through official channels
Enter your full residential address in the official locator. Do not post a child’s name, date of birth, home address, or documents in public questions, community posts, or this website. Ask the district about alternative verification and assistance if documents are missing or you share housing or have temporary accommodation.

A short district inquiry template
Hello, we plan to apply for [grade] in [school year/month] and have checked your official address locator. Should we use new-student enrollment, an intradistrict school change, or an interdistrict transfer? What documents are needed, and how do we confirm school placement and the start date? We would also like information about [language/learning/after-school care] support.

Use the intended grade and the boundary version for the correct school year.
Check the high-school district separately instead of reusing an elementary result.
Save formal enrollment confirmation and check the schedule or first-day arrangements.

title: East Bay schools: verify the address, then find the right enrollment office
summary: Verify the responsible district by full address and grade, distinguish new enrollment from transfers within or between districts, and find school visits, UC Berkeley and Peralta college entry points.
keywords: East Bay schools: verify the address, then find the right enrollment office
content:
There is no single enrollment system for every East Bay city. Confirm the county and full address, identify the district serving your child's grade, then compare school programs. County directories are starting points, not enrollment forms that assign schools, and this guide does not rank schools.

Check the address and grade together

In Alameda County, start with ACOE's school and district directory and map; in Contra Costa County, use CCCOE's district directory to reach district websites. Check the district boundary with the full street address, then use that district's School Locator for individual schools. Elementary, middle and high schools may be served by different districts. City names, ZIP codes and property-site labels do not replace verification. Ask the enrollment office about new streets, boundary addresses or unclear map results.

Continue through the appropriate district entry point

Oakland: ChooseOUSD searches schools by grade and address, with applications through EnrollWise. For immediate current-year enrollment, contact the Enrollment Office to confirm the current process.
Berkeley: the Admissions Office manages enrollment and assignment. Check elementary and middle school zones separately and use the relevant grade-level process; a zone does not guarantee one particular school.
Fremont: the new-student Aeries enrollment account is separate from Parent Portal. Ask the district to verify an unrecognized address. The page still contains older school-year wording, so confirm the correct year and follow-up appointment steps before submitting.
Mt. Diablo: use the Enrollment Center's School Finder for the address and grade, then follow centralized enrollment. The map is a guide; confirm special boundary cases and the final school with the district.
San Ramon Valley: use the School Site Locator, prepare documents, apply online and complete review. The district notes that schools or grade levels may be full; an address-based school is not a guaranteed seat.

Handle enrollment, transfers and school visits separately

At review, Berkeley, Mt. Diablo and San Ramon Valley provided 2026–27 enrollment entry points; recheck the calendar for the next school year. New families should use official lists for residency, age and educational records and submit documents only through official channels. For a school change within a district, check intradistrict procedures; across districts, check interdistrict procedures with both districts for permits, seats and decision timing. A submitted application is not a completed assignment.

Use the district's school directory to reach school websites and book visits. Ask about language and learning support, classes, after-school care and transport. Obtain permission before entering a campus. If standard residency documents are missing or interpretation is needed, ask enrollment staff about alternative verification and support; do not send documents to strangers.

Universities and community colleges do not use K–12 assignment

UC Berkeley separates first-year and transfer applicants on its undergraduate application page. Its visit page links to tours and admissions presentations, with separate booking checks. Peralta's enrollment page lists Berkeley City College, College of Alameda, Laney and Merritt: explore each campus and its courses, choose a college, complete enrollment, then register for classes in Campus Solutions. County directories list additional community colleges. Check college eligibility, teaching locations, costs and visits separately; local residence does not establish admission or free tuition.

A message template for the district
I plan [new enrollment / an intradistrict transfer / an interdistrict transfer] for a student in [grade], starting [school year / month]. Please confirm address verification, the responsible district, documents, the current application round, review steps and school visits. I will provide the full address and student documents only through the designated official channel.

Verify the district responsible for each grade using the address.
Distinguish current-year enrollment from next-year applications.
Confirm the transfer type and required permits.
Save receipts and confirm assignment, registration and support with the school.

title: North Bay schools and districts: separate starting points for Marin, Sonoma, and Napa
summary: The North Bay is not one school district. Use each county’s directory, then check grade, school year, transfers, student support, and school or community-college visits.
keywords: North Bay schools and districts: separate starting points for Marin, Sonoma, and Napa
content:
The North Bay spans Marin, Sonoma, and Napa counties. Individual districts handle enrollment; there is no single North Bay application. Start with the county, then use the actual address, grade, and school year. Neither the city name nor the nearest school determines assignment. County education directories help locate the right district, which confirms placement.

How to check each county

Marin: the official district page provides address or parcel boundary lookup and lists elementary, high-school, and unified districts separately. Elementary and high-school districts may differ; save both results and consult the directory for the intended grade.
Sonoma: enter District Lookup from the SCOE directory, then confirm school attendance boundaries with the district. District boundaries and individual school attendance areas are separate checks; a county map alone does not establish a campus assignment.
Napa: the NCOE directory lists NVUSD, St. Helena, Calistoga, and other districts; NVUSD does not cover the entire county. If the address belongs to NVUSD, follow its registration page to School of Residence. When the interactive map carries an update notice, confirm the result with the district.

Confirm the school year before arranging enrollment and support

After identifying the district, clarify whether this is current-year enrollment or a next-year application, then obtain the correct document checklist, submission channel, and review contact. Old dates or system-maintenance notices do not establish that enrollment is unavailable. If Napa page sections refer to different years, confirm with the registration office before using an old window. Intradistrict and interdistrict transfers have separate processes; Sonoma guidance makes clear that acceptance is not automatic, so follow both sending and receiving decisions.

New families can ask about language assessment, interpretation, counselors, and family communication tools. For an existing learning-support plan, ask how records can be transferred securely. Arrange school visits through the official directory and office, and check pickup procedures, after-school eligibility and fees, and whether transportation serves the address. A neighbor’s arrangements are not a countywide standard.

Community colleges have separate application and campus resources

At College of Marin, arrange a Kentfield or Indian Valley visit and choose the appropriate applicant type through Apply. SRJC admissions lists Santa Rosa and Petaluma service locations; check campus-tour bookings separately. Napa Valley College’s Admissions & Aid page links to new-student steps, the Welcome Center, and campus maps. Confirm college application, course registration, and fees by student type and program. K–12 district assignment does not apply, and course space or transfer admission is not guaranteed.

Enter addresses only through official channels
Enter your full residential address in the official locator. Do not post a child’s name, date of birth, home address, or documents in public questions, community posts, or this website. Ask the district about alternative verification and assistance if documents are missing or you share housing or have temporary accommodation.

A short district inquiry template
Hello, we plan to apply for [grade] in [school year/month] and have checked your official address locator. Should we use new-student enrollment, an intradistrict school change, or an interdistrict transfer? What documents are needed, and how do we confirm school placement and the start date? We would also like information about [language/learning/after-school care] support.

Confirm the county, district, grade, and relevant school year.
Resolve map questions with the district instead of inferring from a city name.
Save enrollment review or transfer decisions and confirm the receiving school and start date.
Check language support, transportation, after-school care, and costs in advance.
